workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Task id or glob passed to tb -t (e.g. hello-world, crack-7z-hash*, * for the full dataset)'
        required: false
        default: 'hello-world'
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1471: default = todays behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'gh-1471 D1/AC 2a: ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Dataset spec passed to tb -d (name==version)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench-core==0.1.1'
      shards:
        description: 'Matrix shard count (10 tasks/shard on the 80-task core dataset)'
        required: false
        default: '8'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared caps, median 360s)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      test-timeout-floor:
        description: 'Floor for declared task test timeouts, seconds (gh-1206; 0 = declared budgets)'
        required: false
        default: '120'
      max-concurrent:
        description: 'Shard jobs running at once (issue #1392: split 8, run 2 — the ours-vs-endpoint experiment; GHA queues the rest)'
        required: false
        default: '2'

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds up to 5 runners for hours; queue a second
# dispatch instead of stacking them.
concurrency:
  group: bench
  cancel-in-progress: false

# One source of truth for the bench model id (PR #1351 review): the run
# config and both summary steps must never drift apart — a stale copy is
# exactly the silent mispricing AC3 of issue #1339 fixes. (The job name
# cannot read this context — see the note on `name:` below.)
env:
  BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & resolve shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Round-3 review: validate max-concurrent like its siblings — 0 or
      # negative would spin the whole matrix as effectively unbounded
      # (and poison FA_BENCH_CONCURRENCY / the packing budget); fail the
      # dispatch BEFORE any bundle is built. (A non-integer value still
      # dies at workflow-graph parse — strategy.max-parallel fromJSON —
      # before any job starts; this guard catches everything numeric.)
      - name: Validate max-concurrent
        run: |
          case "${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}" in
            ''|*[!0-9]*)
              echo "::error::max-concurrent must be a positive integer, got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -lt 1 ] || [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -gt 8 ]; then
            echo "::error::max-concurrent must be between 1 and 8 (the split count), got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1
          fi

      # gh-1471: map the provider choice to the full provider triple
      # (type/baseUrl/model/key env) and preflight the selected secret
      # BEFORE the bundle builds or any shard starts — a missing
      # FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY must cost one setup minute, not 8 shards × hours
      # of 429s. Presence only: the value is never echoed (the ::add-mask
      # line masks its base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into
      # the container). An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a
      # silent fallthrough to the zai default.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1
              fi
              # Key-like fields hard-fail: a pasted key in a dispatch
              # input would leak through run metadata. Whole-word match
              # on the key's split words (camelCase/snake_case divided) —
              # so the legitimate `maxTokens` capability key passes while
              # `token`/`accessToken`/`api_key` are caught.
              leaked=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '
                def words: gsub("(?<l>[a-z0-9])(?<u>[A-Z])"; "\(.l)_\(.u)")
                  | gsub("[ _-]+"; " ") | ascii_downcase | split(" ");
                [keys[]
                  | select(. | words
                      | map(test("^(api.?key|apikey|key|token|secret)$"))
                      | any)]
                  | join(", ")')
              if [ -n "$leaked" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must not carry key material — dispatch inputs are visible in run metadata; offending field(s): $leaked. The key comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret"; exit 1
              fi
              # Required: a non-empty https:// baseUrl and a model — the
              # plain-http ban keeps the bench key off a cleartext wire.
              for field in baseUrl model; do
                if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e --arg f "$field" '.[$f] | type == "string" and length > 0' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                  echo "::error::provider-config is missing a non-empty \"$field\" — required: baseUrl, model"; exit 1
                fi
              done
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e '.baseUrl | startswith("https://")' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config baseUrl must start with https:// (a plaintext endpoint would expose the bench key) — got: $(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.baseUrl')"; exit 1
              fi
              # Verbatim passthrough (every declared field rides the
              # config) plus the fixed key-env injection; `type` defaults
              # to the openai-compatible catalog entry.
              provider_type=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.type // "openai"')
              model=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -r '.model')
              provider_config=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -c --arg k "$key_env" '. + {apiKeyEnvVar: $k}')
              run_label="custom ($model)"
              ;;
            *)
              echo "::error::unknown provider '$PROVIDER' — expected 'zai-glm-5.3-flash', 'kimi-for-coding' or 'custom'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ -z "$secret_value" ]; then
            echo "::error::provider $PROVIDER selected but secret $secret_name is not set"; exit 1
          fi
          # fa_agent.py ships the key into the container base64-encoded;
          # GitHub auto-masks only the raw value, so mask the base64 form.
          echo "::add-mask::$(printf %s "$secret_value" | base64 -w0)"
          {
            echo "provider_type=$provider_type"
            echo "provider_config=$provider_config"
            echo "provider_key_env=$key_env"
            echo "bench_model=$model"
            echo "run_label=$run_label"
          } >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      # stable satisfies the repo SDK constraint (>=3.12.0 <4.0.0).

Senior Developer Engineer focused on code fixes You are an agent triggered to perform a specific task. All required context — ticket description, PR diff, CI status, and related materials — has already been prepared in the `input/` folder. Your job is to follow the instructions below, read the prepared context from `input/`, and perform the work described. Do not ask for identifiers; the context is already available locally. ```mermaid flowchart TD G1["⚠️ Coding Guidelines — follow existing codebase patterns and conventions"] G2["Before implementing, explore the project's code structure, architecture, and testing patterns"] G3["If AGENTS.md exists in project root or subdirectories → READ and FOLLOW it — it contains agent-specific instructions, coding styles, and conventions"] G4["If skills are available in the project → USE them — they provide specialized capabilities, workflows, and tool integrations"] G5["Instructions may be extended via project configuration — always follow the full set of provided instructions"] G6["Never invent new patterns when the codebase already has an established way of doing things"] G1 --> G2 --> G3 --> G4 --> G5 --> G6 ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD START([Ticket enters rework]) --> SETUP{rework_setup_failed.md exists?} SETUP -->|Yes| FAIL[Write setup failure response and stop] SETUP -->|No| INPUT[Read ALL input files in the ticket subfolder] INPUT --> INPUTS["request.md, comments.md, existing_questions.json, parent_context_*.md, pr_info.md, pr_diff.txt, merge_conflicts.md, ci_failures.md, ci_failures_full.log, review_state.md, pr_discussions.md, pr_discussions_raw.json"] INPUTS --> CONFLICTS{merge_conflicts.md exists?} CONFLICTS -->|Yes| RESOLVE["Resolve every conflict marker, git add each file, verify with git diff --check"] CONFLICTS -->|No| CI RESOLVE --> CI{ci_failures.md or ci_failures_full.log exists?} CI -->|Yes| FIX_CI["Fix CI root cause: dependencies, config, or test setup"] CI -->|No| THREADS FIX_CI --> THREADS[Address every open thread in pr_discussions.md] THREADS --> BLOCKING{BLOCKING issues?} BLOCKING -->|Yes| FIX_BLOCK["Fix BLOCKING first — security, critical bugs"] FIX_BLOCK --> IMPORTANT BLOCKING -->|No| IMPORTANT[Fix IMPORTANT issues] IMPORTANT --> SUGGESTIONS{Minor suggestions?} SUGGESTIONS -->|Yes| SKIP["Skip if time-consuming — note in response.md"] SUGGESTIONS -->|No| TEST["Follow TDD approach for every fix — see tdd_approach.md — then run tests and verify"] SKIP --> TEST TEST --> OUTPUT[Write outputs/response.md] OUTPUT --> REPLIES{Open review threads?} REPLIES -->|Yes| REVIEW_REPLIES["Write outputs/review_replies.json with one reply per open thread using threadId + inReplyToId"] REPLIES -->|No| END([End]) REVIEW_REPLIES --> END ``` ## 1. Input context — MANDATORY reading order ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph PR_CONTEXT["⚠️ PR-specific files (read first)"] P1["1️⃣ instruction.md (repo root) — project stack, conventions"] P2["2️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_info.md — PR title, author, branch, description"] P3["3️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_diff.txt — the diff to review"] P4["4️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_files.txt — list of changed files"] P5["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures.md — CI failures = BLOCKING (last 500 lines)"] P5_FULL["5️⃣ input/TICKET/ci_failures_full.log — full CI logs"] P6["6️⃣ input/TICKET/review_state.md — reviewer verdict + decision state (CHANGES_REQUESTED = blocking)"] P7["7️⃣ input/TICKET/pr_discussions.md + pr_discussions_raw.json — existing comments"] P1 --> P2 --> P3 --> P4 --> P5 --> P5_FULL --> P6 --> P7 end subgraph TICKET_CONTEXT["Ticket context (for understanding PR purpose)"] T1["7️⃣ input/TICKET/ticket.md — linked ticket description, ACs"] T2["8️⃣ input/TICKET/comments.md — ticket discussion if present"] T3["9️⃣ input/TICKET/parent-*.md — parent story context"] T4["🔟 input/TICKET/confluence/*.md — linked specifications"] T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 end subgraph RULE["⚠️ Rule"] R1["If file exists in input/ → read locally, do NOT re-fetch via dmtools"] end PR_CONTEXT --> TICKET_CONTEXT --> RULE ``` Read PR files to understand WHAT changed. Read ticket files to understand WHY it changed and verify against requirements. ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph TDD["TDD for PR Rework — RED-GREEN-REFACTOR"] T0["Start from the concrete issue: a CI failure, a review thread, or a BLOCKING/IMPORTANT finding"] T1["RED: Write or extend a test that REPRODUCES the reported issue
— must fail before the fix
— cover the exact scenario called out (including boundary/multi-item cases, not just the happy path)"] T2["GREEN: Make the minimum code change to turn the test PASS
— do not expand scope beyond the reported issue"] T3["REFACTOR: Clean up while keeping tests GREEN
— run the full test suite after every change"] T4{"More findings to address?"} T5["Repeat RED-GREEN-REFACTOR for the next finding"] T0 --> T1 --> T2 --> T3 --> T4 T4 -->|Yes| T5 --> T1 T4 -->|No| DONE([All findings fixed with regression tests]) end subgraph RULES["PR Rework TDD Rules"] R1["❌ NEVER change production code in response to a review comment or CI failure without a test that first reproduces it"] R2["✅ If the existing tests only cover a single-item/simple case, add a test for the multi-item/edge case the finding points at — a fix without a test for that exact case is not verified"] R3["✅ Returned findings: your fix must differ from the previous attempt and the new/updated test must prove it"] R4["✅ Run the FULL test suite before finishing — no regressions allowed"] R5["✅ Verification order: finalize ALL fixes BEFORE launching the full test-suite/coverage run — a run over a tree you are still editing is wasted"] R6["✅ Long runs (full suite, coverage) start with bash background: true and are collected via bash_job status/output between other steps — NEVER foreground sleep-polling (see prompts/bash_tools.md)"] R7["❌ NEVER kill a running verification because files changed after it started — let it finish, treat the result as stale, re-run deliberately"] end TDD --> RULES ``` ```mermaid flowchart TD F1["outputs/response.md must be Markdown (# headings, - bullets, ``` code fences)"] F2["Required sections: ## Issues/Notes (if any), ## Approach, ## Files Modified, ## Test Coverage"] F3["Be surgical but thorough — fix exact issues flagged, then check same pattern across codebase"] F4["Do NOT refactor unrelated code or add unrequested features"] F5["When open PR review threads exist, create outputs/review_replies/*.md files and reference them from outputs/review_replies.json"] ``` - When `input//pr_discussions_raw.json` contains open PR review threads: - Write one Markdown file per open thread under `outputs/review_replies/`. - Write `outputs/review_replies.json` with one entry per open thread, including `inReplyToId`, `threadId`, and a `reply` field that contains the path to the matching `.md` file. - # Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1475
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1475

- **Deletions**: -55

## PR Description

workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Task id or glob passed to tb -t (e.g. hello-world, crack-7z-hash*, * for the full dataset)'
        required: false
        default: 'hello-world'
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1471: default = todays behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'gh-1471 D1/AC 2a: ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Dataset spec passed to tb -d (name==version)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench-core==0.1.1'
      shards:
        description: 'Matrix shard count (10 tasks/shard on the 80-task core dataset)'
        required: false
        default: '8'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared caps, median 360s)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      test-timeout-floor:
        description: 'Floor for declared task test timeouts, seconds (gh-1206; 0 = declared budgets)'
        required: false
        default: '120'
      max-concurrent:
        description: 'Shard jobs running at once (issue #1392: split 8, run 2 — the ours-vs-endpoint experiment; GHA queues the rest)'
        required: false
        default: '2'

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds up to 5 runners for hours; queue a second
# dispatch instead of stacking them.
concurrency:
  group: bench
  cancel-in-progress: false

# One source of truth for the bench model id (PR #1351 review): the run
# config and both summary steps must never drift apart — a stale copy is
# exactly the silent mispricing AC3 of issue #1339 fixes. (The job name
# cannot read this context — see the note on `name:` below.)
env:
  BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & resolve shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Round-3 review: validate max-concurrent like its siblings — 0 or
      # negative would spin the whole matrix as effectively unbounded
      # (and poison FA_BENCH_CONCURRENCY / the packing budget); fail the
      # dispatch BEFORE any bundle is built. (A non-integer value still
      # dies at workflow-graph parse — strategy.max-parallel fromJSON —
      # before any job starts; this guard catches everything numeric.)
      - name: Validate max-concurrent
        run: |
          case "${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}" in
            ''|*[!0-9]*)
              echo "::error::max-concurrent must be a positive integer, got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -lt 1 ] || [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -gt 8 ]; then
            echo "::error::max-concurrent must be between 1 and 8 (the split count), got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1
          fi

      # gh-1471: map the provider choice to the full provider triple
      # (type/baseUrl/model/key env) and preflight the selected secret
      # BEFORE the bundle builds or any shard starts — a missing
      # FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY must cost one setup minute, not 8 shards × hours
      # of 429s. Presence only: the value is never echoed (the ::add-mask
      # line masks its base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into
      # the container). An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a
      # silent fallthrough to the zai default.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY

              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)

              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1475
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1475
- **Title**: gh-1471 [GOAL] bench.yml: provider selection for tbench runs (zai-glm default, kimi-for-coding) with a dedicated bench key
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1471` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +916
- **Deletions**: -55
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T06:51:24Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T07:46:17Z

## PR Description

Closes #1471
## What changed

The terminal-bench workflow stops hardcoding the z.ai GLM provider: a new `provider` dispatch choice (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding`) is resolved in the setup job to the full provider triple and preflighted against the selected bench secret before any shard starts; kimi runs on a dedicated `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` (never `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY`) as `kimi` / `api.kimi.com/coding/v1` / `k3-256k`. The `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` env contract now accepts optional `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` (rides the resolver's override layer into the booted model), and the run identity (workflow `run-name`, shard job names via `needs` outputs, summary `Provider:` header via `BENCH_RUN_LABEL`) names provider+model. `bench/pricing.json` gains an explicit zero entry for `k3-256k` with a comment (subscription plan, no published per-token price — never an invented number).

## Key decisions

- Resolve + secret preflight live in the **setup job** (presence check only, key value never echoed; base64 form masked like the shard step's standing contract) — a bad dispatch fails in minute one, burning zero shard-hours; shard jobs consume the resolved outputs via `needs`.
- REG-1: the default choice resolves the exact legacy 3-field zai JSON (`model` still sourced from the `BENCH_MODEL` pin) — pinned byte-for-byte by a UT.
- Shard step maps **both** bench secrets and the run block picks the resolved key by name (`${!FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV}`) — no dynamic `secrets[...]` indexing, block stays env-driven and testable by the existing shell-harness family.
- `contextWindow: 200000` / `maxTokens: 16384` are declared explicitly for kimi (matches the catalog spec today, but immune to catalog drift); undeclared zai boots stay byte-identical.
- Artifact names (`tb-runs-shard-N`) intentionally unchanged — the merge job downloads by that pattern; run identity rides `run-name`/job name/summary header.

## How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench   # 328 tests, incl. new ProviderResolveStepTest + shape tests
dart test test/cli/env_provider_preconfig_test.dart test/model_roles/provider_catalog_test.dart
actionlint .github/workflows/bench.yml                  # clean
```

Owner setup (E2E blocker, not the code): add the repo secret `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`, then smoke `tasks=hello-world, provider=kimi-for-coding, 1 shard`.

Note: `dart test test/cli/` (full dir) passes all 245 tests but the VM aborts in glibc at process shutdown on this runner — reproduced identically on clean `origin/main` (pre-existing environment issue, unrelated to this change).

<details>
<summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  DISP[workflow_dispatch provider choice] --> RES[setup: Resolve provider]
  SEC1[secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY] --> RES
  SEC2[secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY] --> RES
  RES -->|unknown choice / missing secret: [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] fail, zero shard-hours| X1((fail))
  RES -->|outputs: type, config JSON, key env, run_label| SHARD[bench shard jobs]
  SHARD -->|FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG / key by name| AG[fa_agent.py → container env preconfig]
  AG --> MODEL[buildCliDefaultModel: declared contextWindow/maxTokens win]
  SHARD --> SUM[summary.py: Provider: run_label + pinned MODEL]
```

</details>

workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Task id or glob passed to tb -t (e.g. hello-world, crack-7z-hash*, * for the full dataset)'
        required: false
        default: 'hello-world'
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1471: default = todays behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'gh-1471 D1/AC 2a: ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Dataset spec passed to tb -d (name==version)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench-core==0.1.1'
      shards:
        description: 'Matrix shard count (10 tasks/shard on the 80-task core dataset)'
        required: false
        default: '8'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared caps, median 360s)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      test-timeout-floor:
        description: 'Floor for declared task test timeouts, seconds (gh-1206; 0 = declared budgets)'
        required: false
        default: '120'
      max-concurrent:
        description: 'Shard jobs running at once (issue #1392: split 8, run 2 — the ours-vs-endpoint experiment; GHA queues the rest)'
        required: false
        default: '2'

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds up to 5 runners for hours; queue a second
# dispatch instead of stacking them.
concurrency:
  group: bench
  cancel-in-progress: false

# One source of truth for the bench model id (PR #1351 review): the run
# config and both summary steps must never drift apart — a stale copy is
# exactly the silent mispricing AC3 of issue #1339 fixes. (The job name
# cannot read this context — see the note on `name:` below.)
env:
  BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & resolve shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Round-3 review: validate max-concurrent like its siblings — 0 or
      # negative would spin the whole matrix as effectively unbounded
      # (and poison FA_BENCH_CONCURRENCY / the packing budget); fail the
      # dispatch BEFORE any bundle is built. (A non-integer value still
      # dies at workflow-graph parse — strategy.max-parallel fromJSON —
      # before any job starts; this guard catches everything numeric.)
      - name: Validate max-concurrent
        run: |
          case "${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}" in
            ''|*[!0-9]*)
              echo "::error::max-concurrent must be a positive integer, got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -lt 1 ] || [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -gt 8 ]; then
            echo "::error::max-concurrent must be between 1 and 8 (the split count), got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1
          fi

      # gh-1471: map the provider choice to the full provider triple
      # (type/baseUrl/model/key env) and preflight the selected secret
      # BEFORE the bundle builds or any shard starts — a missing
      # FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY must cost one setup minute, not 8 shards × hours
      # of 429s. Presence only: the value is never echoed (the ::add-mask
      # line masks its base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into
      # the container). An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a
      # silent fallthrough to the zai default.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1
              fi

              # so the legitimate `maxTokens` capability key passes while
              # `token`/`accessToken`/`api_key` are caught.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1475
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1475
- **Title**: gh-1471 [GOAL] bench.yml: provider selection for tbench runs (zai-glm default, kimi-for-coding) with a dedicated bench key
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1471` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +916
- **Deletions**: -55
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T06:51:24Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T07:46:17Z

## PR Description

Closes #1471
## What changed

The terminal-bench workflow stops hardcoding the z.ai GLM provider: a new `provider` dispatch choice (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding`) is resolved in the setup job to the full provider triple and preflighted against the selected bench secret before any shard starts; kimi runs on a dedicated `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` (never `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY`) as `kimi` / `api.kimi.com/coding/v1` / `k3-256k`. The `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` env contract now accepts optional `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` (rides the resolver's override layer into the booted model), and the run identity (workflow `run-name`, shard job names via `needs` outputs, summary `Provider:` header via `BENCH_RUN_LABEL`) names provider+model. `bench/pricing.json` gains an explicit zero entry for `k3-256k` with a comment (subscription plan, no published per-token price — never an invented number).

## Key decisions

- Resolve + secret preflight live in the **setup job** (presence check only, key value never echoed; base64 form masked like the shard step's standing contract) — a bad dispatch fails in minute one, burning zero shard-hours; shard jobs consume the resolved outputs via `needs`.
- REG-1: the default choice resolves the exact legacy 3-field zai JSON (`model` still sourced from the `BENCH_MODEL` pin) — pinned byte-for-byte by a UT.
- Shard step maps **both** bench secrets and the run block picks the resolved key by name (`${!FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV}`) — no dynamic `secrets[...]` indexing, block stays env-driven and testable by the existing shell-harness family.
- `contextWindow: 200000` / `maxTokens: 16384` are declared explicitly for kimi (matches the catalog spec today, but immune to catalog drift); undeclared zai boots stay byte-identical.
- Artifact names (`tb-runs-shard-N`) intentionally unchanged — the merge job downloads by that pattern; run identity rides `run-name`/job name/summary header.

## How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench   # 328 tests, incl. new ProviderResolveStepTest + shape tests
dart test test/cli/env_provider_preconfig_test.dart test/model_roles/provider_catalog_test.dart
actionlint .github/workflows/bench.yml                  # clean
```

Owner setup (E2E blocker, not the code): add the repo secret `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`, then smoke `tasks=hello-world, provider=kimi-for-coding, 1 shard`.

Note: `dart test test/cli/` (full dir) passes all 245 tests but the VM aborts in glibc at process shutdown on this runner — reproduced identically on clean `origin/main` (pre-existing environment issue, unrelated to this change).

<details>
<summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  DISP[workflow_dispatch provider choice] --> RES[setup: Resolve provider]
  SEC1[secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY] --> RES
  SEC2[secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY] --> RES
  RES -->|unknown choice / missing secret: [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] fail, zero shard-hours| X1((fail))
  RES -->|outputs: type, config JSON, key env, run_label| SHARD[bench shard jobs]
  SHARD -->|FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG / key by name| AG[fa_agent.py → container env preconfig]
  AG --> MODEL[buildCliDefaultModel: declared contextWindow/maxTokens win]
  SHARD --> SUM[summary.py: Provider: run_label + pinned MODEL]
```

</details>

The terminal-bench workflow stops hardcoding the z.ai GLM provider: a new `provider` dispatch choice (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding`) is resolved in the setup job to the full provider triple and preflighted against the selected bench secret before any shard starts; kimi runs on a dedicated `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` (never `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY`) as `kimi` / `api.kimi.com/coding/v1` / `k3-256k`. workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Task id or glob passed to tb -t (e.g. hello-world, crack-7z-hash*, * for the full dataset)'
        required: false
        default: 'hello-world'
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1471: default = todays behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'gh-1471 D1/AC 2a: ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Dataset spec passed to tb -d (name==version)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench-core==0.1.1'
      shards:
        description: 'Matrix shard count (10 tasks/shard on the 80-task core dataset)'
        required: false
        default: '8'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared caps, median 360s)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      test-timeout-floor:
        description: 'Floor for declared task test timeouts, seconds (gh-1206; 0 = declared budgets)'
        required: false
        default: '120'
      max-concurrent:
        description: 'Shard jobs running at once (issue #1392: split 8, run 2 — the ours-vs-endpoint experiment; GHA queues the rest)'
        required: false
        default: '2'

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds up to 5 runners for hours; queue a second
# dispatch instead of stacking them.
concurrency:
  group: bench
  cancel-in-progress: false

# One source of truth for the bench model id (PR #1351 review): the run
# config and both summary steps must never drift apart — a stale copy is
# exactly the silent mispricing AC3 of issue #1339 fixes. (The job name
# cannot read this context — see the note on `name:` below.)
env:
  BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & resolve shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Round-3 review: validate max-concurrent like its siblings — 0 or
      # negative would spin the whole matrix as effectively unbounded
      # (and poison FA_BENCH_CONCURRENCY / the packing budget); fail the
      # dispatch BEFORE any bundle is built. (A non-integer value still
      # dies at workflow-graph parse — strategy.max-parallel fromJSON —
      # before any job starts; this guard catches everything numeric.)
      - name: Validate max-concurrent
        run: |
          case "${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}" in
            ''|*[!0-9]*)
              echo "::error::max-concurrent must be a positive integer, got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -lt 1 ] || [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -gt 8 ]; then
            echo "::error::max-concurrent must be between 1 and 8 (the split count), got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1
          fi

      # gh-1471: map the provider choice to the full provider triple
      # (type/baseUrl/model/key env) and preflight the selected secret
      # BEFORE the bundle builds or any shard starts — a missing
      # FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY must cost one setup minute, not 8 shards × hours
      # of 429s. Presence only: the value is never echoed (the ::add-mask
      # line masks its base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into
      # the container). An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a
      # silent fallthrough to the zai default.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then
                echo "::error::provider-config must be a JSON object — the raw input is not echoed (it could carry key material)"; exit 1
              fi

              # `token`/`accessToken`/`api_key` are caught.

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1475
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1475
- **Title**: gh-1471 [GOAL] bench.yml: provider selection for tbench runs (zai-glm default, kimi-for-coding) with a dedicated bench key
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1471` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +916
- **Deletions**: -55
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T06:51:24Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T07:46:17Z

## PR Description

Closes #1471
## What changed

The terminal-bench workflow stops hardcoding the z.ai GLM provider: a new `provider` dispatch choice (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding`) is resolved in the setup job to the full provider triple and preflighted against the selected bench secret before any shard starts; kimi runs on a dedicated `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` (never `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY`) as `kimi` / `api.kimi.com/coding/v1` / `k3-256k`. The `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` env contract now accepts optional `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` (rides the resolver's override layer into the booted model), and the run identity (workflow `run-name`, shard job names via `needs` outputs, summary `Provider:` header via `BENCH_RUN_LABEL`) names provider+model. `bench/pricing.json` gains an explicit zero entry for `k3-256k` with a comment (subscription plan, no published per-token price — never an invented number).

## Key decisions

- Resolve + secret preflight live in the **setup job** (presence check only, key value never echoed; base64 form masked like the shard step's standing contract) — a bad dispatch fails in minute one, burning zero shard-hours; shard jobs consume the resolved outputs via `needs`.
- REG-1: the default choice resolves the exact legacy 3-field zai JSON (`model` still sourced from the `BENCH_MODEL` pin) — pinned byte-for-byte by a UT.
- Shard step maps **both** bench secrets and the run block picks the resolved key by name (`${!FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV}`) — no dynamic `secrets[...]` indexing, block stays env-driven and testable by the existing shell-harness family.
- `contextWindow: 200000` / `maxTokens: 16384` are declared explicitly for kimi (matches the catalog spec today, but immune to catalog drift); undeclared zai boots stay byte-identical.
- Artifact names (`tb-runs-shard-N`) intentionally unchanged — the merge job downloads by that pattern; run identity rides `run-name`/job name/summary header.

## How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench   # 328 tests, incl. new ProviderResolveStepTest + shape tests
dart test test/cli/env_provider_preconfig_test.dart test/model_roles/provider_catalog_test.dart
actionlint .github/workflows/bench.yml                  # clean
```

Owner setup (E2E blocker, not the code): add the repo secret `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`, then smoke `tasks=hello-world, provider=kimi-for-coding, 1 shard`.

Note: `dart test test/cli/` (full dir) passes all 245 tests but the VM aborts in glibc at process shutdown on this runner — reproduced identically on clean `origin/main` (pre-existing environment issue, unrelated to this change).

<details>
<summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  DISP[workflow_dispatch provider choice] --> RES[setup: Resolve provider]
  SEC1[secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY] --> RES
  SEC2[secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY] --> RES
  RES -->|unknown choice / missing secret: [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] fail, zero shard-hours| X1((fail))
  RES -->|outputs: type, config JSON, key env, run_label| SHARD[bench shard jobs]
  SHARD -->|FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG / key by name| AG[fa_agent.py → container env preconfig]
  AG --> MODEL[buildCliDefaultModel: declared contextWindow/maxTokens win]
  SHARD --> SUM[summary.py: Provider: run_label + pinned MODEL]
```

</details>

# pr-1475: gh-1471 [GOAL] bench.yml: provider selection for tbench runs (zai-glm default, kimi-for-coding) with a dedicated bench key

## Description

Closes #1471
## What changed

The terminal-bench workflow stops hardcoding the z.ai GLM provider: a new `provider` dispatch choice (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding`) is resolved in the setup job to the full provider triple and preflighted against the selected bench secret before any shard starts; kimi runs on a dedicated `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` (never `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY`) as `kimi` / `api.kimi.com/coding/v1` / `k3-256k`. The `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` env contract now accepts optional `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` (rides the resolver's override layer into the booted model), and the run identity (workflow `run-name`, shard job names via `needs` outputs, summary `Provider:` header via `BENCH_RUN_LABEL`) names provider+model. `bench/pricing.json` gains an explicit zero entry for `k3-256k` with a comment (subscription plan, no published per-token price — never an invented number).

## Key decisions

- Resolve + secret preflight live in the **setup job** (presence check only, key value never echoed; base64 form masked like the shard step's standing contract) — a bad dispatch fails in minute one, burning zero shard-hours; shard jobs consume the resolved outputs via `needs`.
- REG-1: the default choice resolves the exact legacy 3-field zai JSON (`model` still sourced from the `BENCH_MODEL` pin) — pinned byte-for-byte by a UT.
- Shard step maps **both** bench secrets and the run block picks the resolved key by name (`${!FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV}`) — no dynamic `secrets[...]` indexing, block stays env-driven and testable by the existing shell-harness family.
- `contextWindow: 200000` / `maxTokens: 16384` are declared explicitly for kimi (matches the catalog spec today, but immune to catalog drift); undeclared zai boots stay byte-identical.
- Artifact names (`tb-runs-shard-N`) intentionally unchanged — the merge job downloads by that pattern; run identity rides `run-name`/job name/summary header.

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench   # 328 tests, incl. new ProviderResolveStepTest + shape tests
```

workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Task id or glob passed to tb -t (e.g. hello-world, crack-7z-hash*, * for the full dataset)'
        required: false
        default: 'hello-world'
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1471: default = todays behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'gh-1471 D1/AC 2a: ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Dataset spec passed to tb -d (name==version)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench-core==0.1.1'
      shards:
        description: 'Matrix shard count (10 tasks/shard on the 80-task core dataset)'
        required: false
        default: '8'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared caps, median 360s)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      test-timeout-floor:
        description: 'Floor for declared task test timeouts, seconds (gh-1206; 0 = declared budgets)'
        required: false
        default: '120'
      max-concurrent:
        description: 'Shard jobs running at once (issue #1392: split 8, run 2 — the ours-vs-endpoint experiment; GHA queues the rest)'
        required: false
        default: '2'

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds up to 5 runners for hours; queue a second
# dispatch instead of stacking them.
concurrency:
  group: bench
  cancel-in-progress: false

# One source of truth for the bench model id (PR #1351 review): the run
# config and both summary steps must never drift apart — a stale copy is
# exactly the silent mispricing AC3 of issue #1339 fixes. (The job name
# cannot read this context — see the note on `name:` below.)
env:
  BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & resolve shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}

workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Task id or glob passed to tb -t (e.g. hello-world, crack-7z-hash*, * for the full dataset)'
        required: false
        default: 'hello-world'
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1471: default = todays behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'gh-1471 D1/AC 2a: ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Dataset spec passed to tb -d (name==version)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench-core==0.1.1'
      shards:
        description: 'Matrix shard count (10 tasks/shard on the 80-task core dataset)'
        required: false
        default: '8'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared caps, median 360s)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      test-timeout-floor:
        description: 'Floor for declared task test timeouts, seconds (gh-1206; 0 = declared budgets)'
        required: false
        default: '120'
      max-concurrent:
        description: 'Shard jobs running at once (issue #1392: split 8, run 2 — the ours-vs-endpoint experiment; GHA queues the rest)'
        required: false
        default: '2'

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds up to 5 runners for hours; queue a second
# dispatch instead of stacking them.
concurrency:
  group: bench
  cancel-in-progress: false

# One source of truth for the bench model id (PR #1351 review): the run
# config and both summary steps must never drift apart — a stale copy is
# exactly the silent mispricing AC3 of issue #1339 fixes. (The job name
# cannot read this context — see the note on `name:` below.)
env:
  BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & resolve shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Round-3 review: validate max-concurrent like its siblings — 0 or
      # negative would spin the whole matrix as effectively unbounded
      # (and poison FA_BENCH_CONCURRENCY / the packing budget); fail the
      # dispatch BEFORE any bundle is built. (A non-integer value still
      # dies at workflow-graph parse — strategy.max-parallel fromJSON —
      # before any job starts; this guard catches everything numeric.)
      - name: Validate max-concurrent
        run: |
          case "${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}" in
            ''|*[!0-9]*)
              echo "::error::max-concurrent must be a positive integer, got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -lt 1 ] || [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -gt 8 ]; then
            echo "::error::max-concurrent must be between 1 and 8 (the split count), got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1
          fi

      # gh-1471: map the provider choice to the full provider triple
      # (type/baseUrl/model/key env) and preflight the selected secret
      # BEFORE the bundle builds or any shard starts — a missing
      # FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY must cost one setup minute, not 8 shards × hours
      # of 429s. Presence only: the value is never echoed (the ::add-mask
      # line masks its base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into
      # the container). An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a
      # silent fallthrough to the zai default.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi

              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1475
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1475
- **Title**: gh-1471 [GOAL] bench.yml: provider selection for tbench runs (zai-glm default, kimi-for-coding) with a dedicated bench key
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1471` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +916
- **Deletions**: -55
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T06:51:24Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T07:46:17Z

## PR Description

Closes #1471
## What changed

The terminal-bench workflow stops hardcoding the z.ai GLM provider: a new `provider` dispatch choice (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding`) is resolved in the setup job to the full provider triple and preflighted against the selected bench secret before any shard starts; kimi runs on a dedicated `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` (never `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY`) as `kimi` / `api.kimi.com/coding/v1` / `k3-256k`. The `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` env contract now accepts optional `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` (rides the resolver's override layer into the booted model), and the run identity (workflow `run-name`, shard job names via `needs` outputs, summary `Provider:` header via `BENCH_RUN_LABEL`) names provider+model. `bench/pricing.json` gains an explicit zero entry for `k3-256k` with a comment (subscription plan, no published per-token price — never an invented number).

## Key decisions

- Resolve + secret preflight live in the **setup job** (presence check only, key value never echoed; base64 form masked like the shard step's standing contract) — a bad dispatch fails in minute one, burning zero shard-hours; shard jobs consume the resolved outputs via `needs`.
- REG-1: the default choice resolves the exact legacy 3-field zai JSON (`model` still sourced from the `BENCH_MODEL` pin) — pinned byte-for-byte by a UT.
- Shard step maps **both** bench secrets and the run block picks the resolved key by name (`${!FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV}`) — no dynamic `secrets[...]` indexing, block stays env-driven and testable by the existing shell-harness family.
- `contextWindow: 200000` / `maxTokens: 16384` are declared explicitly for kimi (matches the catalog spec today, but immune to catalog drift); undeclared zai boots stay byte-identical.
- Artifact names (`tb-runs-shard-N`) intentionally unchanged — the merge job downloads by that pattern; run identity rides `run-name`/job name/summary header.

## How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench   # 328 tests, incl. new ProviderResolveStepTest + shape tests
dart test test/cli/env_provider_preconfig_test.dart test/model_roles/provider_catalog_test.dart
actionlint .github/workflows/bench.yml                  # clean
```

Owner setup (E2E blocker, not the code): add the repo secret `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`, then smoke `tasks=hello-world, provider=kimi-for-coding, 1 shard`.

Note: `dart test test/cli/` (full dir) passes all 245 tests but the VM aborts in glibc at process shutdown on this runner — reproduced identically on clean `origin/main` (pre-existing environment issue, unrelated to this change).

<details>
<summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  DISP[workflow_dispatch provider choice] --> RES[setup: Resolve provider]
  SEC1[secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY] --> RES
  SEC2[secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY] --> RES
  RES -->|unknown choice / missing secret: [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] fail, zero shard-hours| X1((fail))
  RES -->|outputs: type, config JSON, key env, run_label| SHARD[bench shard jobs]
  SHARD -->|FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG / key by name| AG[fa_agent.py → container env preconfig]
  AG --> MODEL[buildCliDefaultModel: declared contextWindow/maxTokens win]
  SHARD --> SUM[summary.py: Provider: run_label + pinned MODEL]
```

</details>

The `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` env contract now accepts optional `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` (rides the resolver's override layer into the booted model), and the run identity (workflow `run-name`, shard job names via `needs` outputs, summary `Provider:` header via `BENCH_RUN_LABEL`) names provider+model. `bench/pricing.json` gains an explicit zero entry for `k3-256k` with a comment (subscription plan, no published per-token price — never an invented number).

## Key decisions

- Resolve + secret preflight live in the **setup job** (presence check only, key value never echoed; base64 form masked like the shard step's standing contract) — a bad dispatch fails in minute one, burning zero shard-hours; shard jobs consume the resolved outputs via `needs`.

workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Task id or glob passed to tb -t (e.g. hello-world, crack-7z-hash*, * for the full dataset)'
        required: false
        default: 'hello-world'
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1471: default = todays behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'gh-1471 D1/AC 2a: ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Dataset spec passed to tb -d (name==version)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench-core==0.1.1'
      shards:
        description: 'Matrix shard count (10 tasks/shard on the 80-task core dataset)'
        required: false
        default: '8'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared caps, median 360s)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      test-timeout-floor:
        description: 'Floor for declared task test timeouts, seconds (gh-1206; 0 = declared budgets)'
        required: false
        default: '120'
      max-concurrent:
        description: 'Shard jobs running at once (issue #1392: split 8, run 2 — the ours-vs-endpoint experiment; GHA queues the rest)'
        required: false
        default: '2'

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds up to 5 runners for hours; queue a second
# dispatch instead of stacking them.
concurrency:
  group: bench
  cancel-in-progress: false

# One source of truth for the bench model id (PR #1351 review): the run
# config and both summary steps must never drift apart — a stale copy is
# exactly the silent mispricing AC3 of issue #1339 fixes. (The job name
# cannot read this context — see the note on `name:` below.)
env:
  BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & resolve shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Round-3 review: validate max-concurrent like its siblings — 0 or
      # negative would spin the whole matrix as effectively unbounded
      # (and poison FA_BENCH_CONCURRENCY / the packing budget); fail the
      # dispatch BEFORE any bundle is built. (A non-integer value still
      # dies at workflow-graph parse — strategy.max-parallel fromJSON —
      # before any job starts; this guard catches everything numeric.)
      - name: Validate max-concurrent
        run: |
          case "${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}" in
            ''|*[!0-9]*)
              echo "::error::max-concurrent must be a positive integer, got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -lt 1 ] || [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -gt 8 ]; then
            echo "::error::max-concurrent must be between 1 and 8 (the split count), got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1
          fi

      # gh-1471: map the provider choice to the full provider triple
      # (type/baseUrl/model/key env) and preflight the selected secret
      # BEFORE the bundle builds or any shard starts — a missing
      # FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY must cost one setup minute, not 8 shards × hours
      # of 429s. Presence only: the value is never echoed (the ::add-mask
      # line masks its base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into
      # the container). An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a
      # silent fallthrough to the zai default.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1475
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1475
- **Title**: gh-1471 [GOAL] bench.yml: provider selection for tbench runs (zai-glm default, kimi-for-coding) with a dedicated bench key
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1471` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +916
- **Deletions**: -55
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T06:51:24Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T07:46:17Z

## PR Description

Closes #1471
## What changed

The terminal-bench workflow stops hardcoding the z.ai GLM provider: a new `provider` dispatch choice (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding`) is resolved in the setup job to the full provider triple and preflighted against the selected bench secret before any shard starts; kimi runs on a dedicated `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` (never `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY`) as `kimi` / `api.kimi.com/coding/v1` / `k3-256k`. The `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` env contract now accepts optional `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` (rides the resolver's override layer into the booted model), and the run identity (workflow `run-name`, shard job names via `needs` outputs, summary `Provider:` header via `BENCH_RUN_LABEL`) names provider+model. `bench/pricing.json` gains an explicit zero entry for `k3-256k` with a comment (subscription plan, no published per-token price — never an invented number).

## Key decisions

- Resolve + secret preflight live in the **setup job** (presence check only, key value never echoed; base64 form masked like the shard step's standing contract) — a bad dispatch fails in minute one, burning zero shard-hours; shard jobs consume the resolved outputs via `needs`.
- REG-1: the default choice resolves the exact legacy 3-field zai JSON (`model` still sourced from the `BENCH_MODEL` pin) — pinned byte-for-byte by a UT.
- Shard step maps **both** bench secrets and the run block picks the resolved key by name (`${!FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV}`) — no dynamic `secrets[...]` indexing, block stays env-driven and testable by the existing shell-harness family.
- `contextWindow: 200000` / `maxTokens: 16384` are declared explicitly for kimi (matches the catalog spec today, but immune to catalog drift); undeclared zai boots stay byte-identical.
- Artifact names (`tb-runs-shard-N`) intentionally unchanged — the merge job downloads by that pattern; run identity rides `run-name`/job name/summary header.

## How to verify


# pr-1475: gh-1471 [GOAL] bench.yml: provider selection for tbench runs (zai-glm default, kimi-for-coding) with a dedicated bench key

## Description

Closes #1471
## What changed

The terminal-bench workflow stops hardcoding the z.ai GLM provider: a new `provider` dispatch choice (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding`) is resolved in the setup job to the full provider triple and preflighted against the selected bench secret before any shard starts; kimi runs on a dedicated `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` (never `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY`) as `kimi` / `api.kimi.com/coding/v1` / `k3-256k`. The `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` env contract now accepts optional `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` (rides the resolver's override layer into the booted model), and the run identity (workflow `run-name`, shard job names via `needs` outputs, summary `Provider:` header via `BENCH_RUN_LABEL`) names provider+model. `bench/pricing.json` gains an explicit zero entry for `k3-256k` with a comment (subscription plan, no published per-token price — never an invented number).
