# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1475
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1475
- **Title**: gh-1471 [GOAL] bench.yml: provider selection for tbench runs (zai-glm default, kimi-for-coding) with a dedicated bench key
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1471` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +916
- **Deletions**: -55
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T06:51:24Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T07:46:17Z

## PR Description

Closes #1471
## What changed

The terminal-bench workflow stops hardcoding the z.ai GLM provider: a new `provider` dispatch choice (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding`) is resolved in the setup job to the full provider triple and preflighted against the selected bench secret before any shard starts; kimi runs on a dedicated `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` (never `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY`) as `kimi` / `api.kimi.com/coding/v1` / `k3-256k`. The `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` env contract now accepts optional `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` (rides the resolver's override layer into the booted model), and the run identity (workflow `run-name`, shard job names via `needs` outputs, summary `Provider:` header via `BENCH_RUN_LABEL`) names provider+model. `bench/pricing.json` gains an explicit zero entry for `k3-256k` with a comment (subscription plan, no published per-token price — never an invented number).

## Key decisions

- Resolve + secret preflight live in the **setup job** (presence check only, key value never echoed; base64 form masked like the shard step's standing contract) — a bad dispatch fails in minute one, burning zero shard-hours; shard jobs consume the resolved outputs via `needs`.
- REG-1: the default choice resolves the exact legacy 3-field zai JSON (`model` still sourced from the `BENCH_MODEL` pin) — pinned byte-for-byte by a UT.
- Shard step maps **both** bench secrets and the run block picks the resolved key by name (`${!FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV}`) — no dynamic `secrets[...]` indexing, block stays env-driven and testable by the existing shell-harness family.
- `contextWindow: 200000` / `maxTokens: 16384` are declared explicitly for kimi (matches the catalog spec today, but immune to catalog drift); undeclared zai boots stay byte-identical.
- Artifact names (`tb-runs-shard-N`) intentionally unchanged — the merge job downloads by that pattern; run identity rides `run-name`/job name/summary header.

## How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench   # 328 tests, incl. new ProviderResolveStepTest + shape tests
dart test test/cli/env_provider_preconfig_test.dart test/model_roles/provider_catalog_test.dart
actionlint .github/workflows/bench.yml                  # clean
```

Owner setup (E2E blocker, not the code): add the repo secret `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`, then smoke `tasks=hello-world, provider=kimi-for-coding, 1 shard`.

Note: `dart test test/cli/` (full dir) passes all 245 tests but the VM aborts in glibc at process shutdown on this runner — reproduced identically on clean `origin/main` (pre-existing environment issue, unrelated to this change).

<details>
<summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  DISP[workflow_dispatch provider choice] --> RES[setup: Resolve provider]
  SEC1[secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY] --> RES
  SEC2[secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY] --> RES
  RES -->|unknown choice / missing secret: [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] fail, zero shard-hours| X1((fail))
  RES -->|outputs: type, config JSON, key env, run_label| SHARD[bench shard jobs]
  SHARD -->|FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG / key by name| AG[fa_agent.py → container env preconfig]
  AG --> MODEL[buildCliDefaultModel: declared contextWindow/maxTokens win]
  SHARD --> SUM[summary.py: Provider: run_label + pinned MODEL]
```

</details>

The terminal-bench workflow stops hardcoding the z.ai GLM provider: a new `provider` dispatch choice (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding`) is resolved in the setup job to the full provider triple and preflighted against the selected bench secret before any shard starts; kimi runs on a dedicated `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` (never `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY`) as `kimi` / `api.kimi.com/coding/v1` / `k3-256k`. The `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` env contract now accepts optional `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` (rides the resolver's override layer into the booted model), and the run identity (workflow `run-name`, shard job names via `needs` outputs, summary `Provider:` header via `BENCH_RUN_LABEL`) names provider+model. `bench/pricing.json` gains an explicit zero entry for `k3-256k` with a comment (subscription plan, no published per-token price — never an invented number).

## Key decisions

- Resolve + secret preflight live in the **setup job** (presence check only, key value never echoed; base64 form masked like the shard step's standing contract) — a bad dispatch fails in minute one, burning zero shard-hours; shard jobs consume the resolved outputs via `needs`.
- REG-1: the default choice resolves the exact legacy 3-field zai JSON (`model` still sourced from the `BENCH_MODEL` pin) — pinned byte-for-byte by a UT.
- Shard step maps **both** bench secrets and the run block picks the resolved key by name (`${!FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV}`) — no dynamic `secrets[...]` indexing, block stays env-driven and testable by the existing shell-harness family.
- `contextWindow: 200000` / `maxTokens: 16384` are declared explicitly for kimi (matches the catalog spec today, but immune to catalog drift); undeclared zai boots stay byte-identical.
- Artifact names (`tb-runs-shard-N`) intentionally unchanged — the merge job downloads by that pattern; run identity rides `run-name`/job name/summary header.

workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Task id or glob passed to tb -t (e.g. hello-world, crack-7z-hash*, * for the full dataset)'
        required: false
        default: 'hello-world'
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1471: default = todays behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'gh-1471 D1/AC 2a: ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Dataset spec passed to tb -d (name==version)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench-core==0.1.1'
      shards:
        description: 'Matrix shard count (10 tasks/shard on the 80-task core dataset)'
        required: false
        default: '8'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared caps, median 360s)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      test-timeout-floor:
        description: 'Floor for declared task test timeouts, seconds (gh-1206; 0 = declared budgets)'
        required: false
        default: '120'
      max-concurrent:
        description: 'Shard jobs running at once (issue #1392: split 8, run 2 — the ours-vs-endpoint experiment; GHA queues the rest)'
        required: false
        default: '2'

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds up to 5 runners for hours; queue a second
# dispatch instead of stacking them.
concurrency:
  group: bench
  cancel-in-progress: false

# One source of truth for the bench model id (PR #1351 review): the run
# config and both summary steps must never drift apart — a stale copy is
# exactly the silent mispricing AC3 of issue #1339 fixes. (The job name
# cannot read this context — see the note on `name:` below.)
env:
  BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & resolve shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Round-3 review: validate max-concurrent like its siblings — 0 or
      # negative would spin the whole matrix as effectively unbounded
      # (and poison FA_BENCH_CONCURRENCY / the packing budget); fail the
      # dispatch BEFORE any bundle is built. (A non-integer value still
      # dies at workflow-graph parse — strategy.max-parallel fromJSON —
      # before any job starts; this guard catches everything numeric.)
      - name: Validate max-concurrent
        run: |
          case "${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}" in
            ''|*[!0-9]*)
              echo "::error::max-concurrent must be a positive integer, got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -lt 1 ] || [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -gt 8 ]; then
            echo "::error::max-concurrent must be between 1 and 8 (the split count), got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1
          fi

      # gh-1471: map the provider choice to the full provider triple
      # (type/baseUrl/model/key env) and preflight the selected secret
      # BEFORE the bundle builds or any shard starts — a missing
      # FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY must cost one setup minute, not 8 shards × hours
      # of 429s. Presence only: the value is never echoed (the ::add-mask
      # line masks its base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into
      # the container). An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a
      # silent fallthrough to the zai default.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY

### Thread 4 — `.github/workflows/bench.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the custom path's `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` is rejected by the Dart env preconfig — every custom trial dies at container boot**

The custom arm builds the shard config with a verbatim passthrough plus the fixed key-env injection (line 280):

```bash
provider_config=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -c --arg k "$key_env" '. + {apiKeyEnvVar: $k}')
```

For the **documented** input shape (`provider-config: {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}`, per the input description and pinned by `test_custom_provider_config_flows_verbatim_with_fixed_key_env`), this produces:

```json
{"type":"openai","baseUrl":"https://api.example.com/v1","model":"m-1","contextWindow":128000,"maxTokens":8192,"apiKeyEnvVar":"FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM"}
```

The Dart consumer does not accept a `type` key inside `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` — `_supportedConfigKeys` is `baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar, contextWindow, maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel` only. Verified against this branch:

```
ConfigException: unknown FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG key: "type" — supported keys: baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar, contextWindow, maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel
  package:flutter_agent_harness/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart  _takeConfigEntry
```

And `faProviderPreconfig`'s contract is deliberate: *"a container that names its provider wrong must fail loud at boot"* — so a custom dispatch burns a whole shard of trials that all fail at fa boot. The run only works if the user **omits** `type` (then `.type // "openai"` sets `provider_type` with no `type` key in the JSON) — i.e. the opposite of the documented example.

Two sound fixes (pick one):

1. **Strip `type` in the passthrough** — it already rides the dedicated `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE` output/env:
   ```bash
   provider_config=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -c --arg k "$key_env" 'del(.type) + {apiKeyEnvVar: $k}')
   ```
2. **Accept `type` Dart-side** — add it to `_supportedConfigKeys` and cross-check it equals the resolved `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE` (a mismatch would be a loud misconfiguration).

Either way, add one cross-layer test: feed the workflow resolve step's actual `provider_config` output into `parseEnvProviderPreconfig` (the two sides are currently pinned by separate tests with opposite expectations — which is exactly how this slipped through).

---

### Thread 5 — `.github/workflows/bench.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the custom preflight doesn't cover the config keys the Dart consumer will enforce — a bad dispatch burns shard-hours, not one setup minute**

The resolve step validates parseability, `baseUrl`/`model`, https-only, and key-like field names (all good), but the config then flows **verbatim** into `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`, where the Dart `_parseConfig` enforces a closed whitelist with typed validators:

- any key outside `baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar, contextWindow, maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel` (e.g. a typo'd `"baseurl"`, or an `"organization"` a provider doc suggested) passes this preflight and fails **loud inside every trial** after shards start;
- `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` below the resolver floors (`minOverrideContextWindow` 16384 / `minOverrideMaxTokens`) likewise pass preflight and throw at container boot;
- `.type` is used unchecked: `{"type": 123}` or `{"type": ""}` yields `provider_type` garbage/empty (jq `//` treats `""` as present) → the catalog lookup fails in the container instead of minute one.

The PR's own design goal is "a bad dispatch fails in minute one, burning zero shard-hours" — a one-block jq check at resolve time closes the gap (whitelist the keys, integer+floor the capability pair, string-check `type` when present), and would have made the `type`-key clash in the sibling finding impossible to miss. While there: the key-like scan only inspects top-level `keys[]` — a key nested inside an object value (e.g. `"headers": {"apiKey": [REDACTED:Sensitive Value]}`) rides through; scanning `.. | objects | keys[]` is a cheap widening (values can smuggle data regardless, but field-name paste accidents are what D1 targets).

# Pull Request Information

- **PR #**: 1475
- **URL**: https://github.com/IstiN/flutter_agent_harness/pull/1475
- **Title**: gh-1471 [GOAL] bench.yml: provider selection for tbench runs (zai-glm default, kimi-for-coding) with a dedicated bench key
- **Author**: ai-teammate
- **Branch**: `ai/gh-1471` → `main`
- **State**: open
- **Files Changed**: 12
- **Additions**: +916
- **Deletions**: -55
- **Created**: 2026-10-10T06:51:24Z
- **Updated**: 2026-10-10T07:46:17Z

## PR Description

Closes #1471
## What changed

The terminal-bench workflow stops hardcoding the z.ai GLM provider: a new `provider` dispatch choice (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding`) is resolved in the setup job to the full provider triple and preflighted against the selected bench secret before any shard starts; kimi runs on a dedicated `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` (never `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY`) as `kimi` / `api.kimi.com/coding/v1` / `k3-256k`. The `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` env contract now accepts optional `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` (rides the resolver's override layer into the booted model), and the run identity (workflow `run-name`, shard job names via `needs` outputs, summary `Provider:` header via `BENCH_RUN_LABEL`) names provider+model. `bench/pricing.json` gains an explicit zero entry for `k3-256k` with a comment (subscription plan, no published per-token price — never an invented number).

## Key decisions

- Resolve + secret preflight live in the **setup job** (presence check only, key value never echoed; base64 form masked like the shard step's standing contract) — a bad dispatch fails in minute one, burning zero shard-hours; shard jobs consume the resolved outputs via `needs`.
- REG-1: the default choice resolves the exact legacy 3-field zai JSON (`model` still sourced from the `BENCH_MODEL` pin) — pinned byte-for-byte by a UT.
- Shard step maps **both** bench secrets and the run block picks the resolved key by name (`${!FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV}`) — no dynamic `secrets[...]` indexing, block stays env-driven and testable by the existing shell-harness family.
- `contextWindow: 200000` / `maxTokens: 16384` are declared explicitly for kimi (matches the catalog spec today, but immune to catalog drift); undeclared zai boots stay byte-identical.
- Artifact names (`tb-runs-shard-N`) intentionally unchanged — the merge job downloads by that pattern; run identity rides `run-name`/job name/summary header.

## How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench   # 328 tests, incl. new ProviderResolveStepTest + shape tests
dart test test/cli/env_provider_preconfig_test.dart test/model_roles/provider_catalog_test.dart
actionlint .github/workflows/bench.yml                  # clean
```

Owner setup (E2E blocker, not the code): add the repo secret `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`, then smoke `tasks=hello-world, provider=kimi-for-coding, 1 shard`.

Note: `dart test test/cli/` (full dir) passes all 245 tests but the VM aborts in glibc at process shutdown on this runner — reproduced identically on clean `origin/main` (pre-existing environment issue, unrelated to this change).

<details>
<summary>Architecture diagram</summary>

```mermaid
flowchart TD
  DISP[workflow_dispatch provider choice] --> RES[setup: Resolve provider]
  SEC1[secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY] --> RES
  SEC2[secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY] --> RES
  RES -->|unknown choice / missing secret: [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] fail, zero shard-hours| X1((fail))
  RES -->|outputs: type, config JSON, key env, run_label| SHARD[bench shard jobs]
  SHARD -->|FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG / key by name| AG[fa_agent.py → container env preconfig]
  AG --> MODEL[buildCliDefaultModel: declared contextWindow/maxTokens win]
  SHARD --> SUM[summary.py: Provider: run_label + pinned MODEL]
```

</details>

# pr-1475: gh-1471 [GOAL] bench.yml: provider selection for tbench runs (zai-glm default, kimi-for-coding) with a dedicated bench key

## Description

Closes #1471
## What changed

The terminal-bench workflow stops hardcoding the z.ai GLM provider: a new `provider` dispatch choice (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding`) is resolved in the setup job to the full provider triple and preflighted against the selected bench secret before any shard starts; kimi runs on a dedicated `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` (never `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY`) as `kimi` / `api.kimi.com/coding/v1` / `k3-256k`. The `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` env contract now accepts optional `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` (rides the resolver's override layer into the booted model), and the run identity (workflow `run-name`, shard job names via `needs` outputs, summary `Provider:` header via `BENCH_RUN_LABEL`) names provider+model. `bench/pricing.json` gains an explicit zero entry for `k3-256k` with a comment (subscription plan, no published per-token price — never an invented number).

## Key decisions

- Resolve + secret preflight live in the **setup job** (presence check only, key value never echoed; base64 form masked like the shard step's standing contract) — a bad dispatch fails in minute one, burning zero shard-hours; shard jobs consume the resolved outputs via `needs`.
- REG-1: the default choice resolves the exact legacy 3-field zai JSON (`model` still sourced from the `BENCH_MODEL` pin) — pinned byte-for-byte by a UT.
- Shard step maps **both** bench secrets and the run block picks the resolved key by name (`${!FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV}`) — no dynamic `secrets[...]` indexing, block stays env-driven and testable by the existing shell-harness family.
- `contextWindow: 200000` / `maxTokens: 16384` are declared explicitly for kimi (matches the catalog spec today, but immune to catalog drift); undeclared zai boots stay byte-identical.
- Artifact names (`tb-runs-shard-N`) intentionally unchanged — the merge job downloads by that pattern; run identity rides `run-name`/job name/summary header.

## How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench   # 328 tests, incl. new ProviderResolveStepTest + shape tests

workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Task id or glob passed to tb -t (e.g. hello-world, crack-7z-hash*, * for the full dataset)'
        required: false
        default: 'hello-world'
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1471: default = todays behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'gh-1471 D1/AC 2a: ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Dataset spec passed to tb -d (name==version)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench-core==0.1.1'
      shards:
        description: 'Matrix shard count (10 tasks/shard on the 80-task core dataset)'
        required: false
        default: '8'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared caps, median 360s)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      test-timeout-floor:
        description: 'Floor for declared task test timeouts, seconds (gh-1206; 0 = declared budgets)'
        required: false
        default: '120'
      max-concurrent:
        description: 'Shard jobs running at once (issue #1392: split 8, run 2 — the ours-vs-endpoint experiment; GHA queues the rest)'
        required: false
        default: '2'

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds up to 5 runners for hours; queue a second
# dispatch instead of stacking them.
concurrency:
  group: bench
  cancel-in-progress: false

# One source of truth for the bench model id (PR #1351 review): the run
# config and both summary steps must never drift apart — a stale copy is
# exactly the silent mispricing AC3 of issue #1339 fixes. (The job name
# cannot read this context — see the note on `name:` below.)
env:
  BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & resolve shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Round-3 review: validate max-concurrent like its siblings — 0 or
      # negative would spin the whole matrix as effectively unbounded
      # (and poison FA_BENCH_CONCURRENCY / the packing budget); fail the
      # dispatch BEFORE any bundle is built. (A non-integer value still
      # dies at workflow-graph parse — strategy.max-parallel fromJSON —
      # before any job starts; this guard catches everything numeric.)
      - name: Validate max-concurrent
        run: |
          case "${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}" in
            ''|*[!0-9]*)
              echo "::error::max-concurrent must be a positive integer, got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -lt 1 ] || [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -gt 8 ]; then
            echo "::error::max-concurrent must be between 1 and 8 (the split count), got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1
          fi

      # gh-1471: map the provider choice to the full provider triple
      # (type/baseUrl/model/key env) and preflight the selected secret
      # BEFORE the bundle builds or any shard starts — a missing
      # FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY must cost one setup minute, not 8 shards × hours
      # of 429s. Presence only: the value is never echoed (the ::add-mask
      # line masks its base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into
      # the container). An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a
      # silent fallthrough to the zai default.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 4 — `.github/workflows/bench.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the custom path's `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` is rejected by the Dart env preconfig — every custom trial dies at container boot**

The custom arm builds the shard config with a verbatim passthrough plus the fixed key-env injection (line 280):

```bash
provider_config=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -c --arg k "$key_env" '. + {apiKeyEnvVar: $k}')
```

For the **documented** input shape (`provider-config: {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}`, per the input description and pinned by `test_custom_provider_config_flows_verbatim_with_fixed_key_env`), this produces:

```json
{"type":"openai","baseUrl":"https://api.example.com/v1","model":"m-1","contextWindow":128000,"maxTokens":8192,"apiKeyEnvVar":"FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM"}
```

The Dart consumer does not accept a `type` key inside `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` — `_supportedConfigKeys` is `baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar, contextWindow, maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel` only. Verified against this branch:

```
ConfigException: unknown FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG key: "type" — supported keys: baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar, contextWindow, maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel
  package:flutter_agent_harness/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart  _takeConfigEntry
```

And `faProviderPreconfig`'s contract is deliberate: *"a container that names its provider wrong must fail loud at boot"* — so a custom dispatch burns a whole shard of trials that all fail at fa boot. The run only works if the user **omits** `type` (then `.type // "openai"` sets `provider_type` with no `type` key in the JSON) — i.e. the opposite of the documented example.

Two sound fixes (pick one):

1. **Strip `type` in the passthrough** — it already rides the dedicated `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE` output/env:
   ```bash
   provider_config=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -c --arg k "$key_env" 'del(.type) + {apiKeyEnvVar: $k}')
   ```
2. **Accept `type` Dart-side** — add it to `_supportedConfigKeys` and cross-check it equals the resolved `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE` (a mismatch would be a loud misconfiguration).

Either way, add one cross-layer test: feed the workflow resolve step's actual `provider_config` output into `parseEnvProviderPreconfig` (the two sides are currently pinned by separate tests with opposite expectations — which is exactly how this slipped through).

---

### Thread 5 — `.github/workflows/bench.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the custom preflight doesn't cover the config keys the Dart consumer will enforce — a bad dispatch burns shard-hours, not one setup minute**

The resolve step validates parseability, `baseUrl`/`model`, https-only, and key-like field names (all good), but the config then flows **verbatim** into `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`, where the Dart `_parseConfig` enforces a closed whitelist with typed validators:

- any key outside `baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar, contextWindow, maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel` (e.g. a typo'd `"baseurl"`, or an `"organization"` a provider doc suggested) passes this preflight and fails **loud inside every trial** after shards start;
- `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` below the resolver floors (`minOverrideContextWindow` 16384 / `minOverrideMaxTokens`) likewise pass preflight and throw at container boot;
- `.type` is used unchecked: `{"type": 123}` or `{"type": ""}` yields `provider_type` garbage/empty (jq `//` treats `""` as present) → the catalog lookup fails in the container instead of minute one.

The PR's own design goal is "a bad dispatch fails in minute one, burning zero shard-hours" — a one-block jq check at resolve time closes the gap (whitelist the keys, integer+floor the capability pair, string-check `type` when present), and would have made the `type`-key clash in the sibling finding impossible to miss. While there: the key-like scan only inspects top-level `keys[]` — a key nested inside an object value (e.g. `"headers": {"apiKey": [REDACTED:Sensitive Value]}`) rides through; scanning `.. | objects | keys[]` is a cheap widening (values can smuggle data regardless, but field-name paste accidents are what D1 targets).

## PR Description

Closes #1471
## What changed

The terminal-bench workflow stops hardcoding the z.ai GLM provider: a new `provider` dispatch choice (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding`) is resolved in the setup job to the full provider triple and preflighted against the selected bench secret before any shard starts; kimi runs on a dedicated `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` (never `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY`) as `kimi` / `api.kimi.com/coding/v1` / `k3-256k`. The `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` env contract now accepts optional `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` (rides the resolver's override layer into the booted model), and the run identity (workflow `run-name`, shard job names via `needs` outputs, summary `Provider:` header via `BENCH_RUN_LABEL`) names provider+model. `bench/pricing.json` gains an explicit zero entry for `k3-256k` with a comment (subscription plan, no published per-token price — never an invented number).

## Key decisions

- Resolve + secret preflight live in the **setup job** (presence check only, key value never echoed; base64 form masked like the shard step's standing contract) — a bad dispatch fails in minute one, burning zero shard-hours; shard jobs consume the resolved outputs via `needs`.
- REG-1: the default choice resolves the exact legacy 3-field zai JSON (`model` still sourced from the `BENCH_MODEL` pin) — pinned byte-for-byte by a UT.
- Shard step maps **both** bench secrets and the run block picks the resolved key by name (`${!FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV}`) — no dynamic `secrets[...]` indexing, block stays env-driven and testable by the existing shell-harness family.
- `contextWindow: 200000` / `maxTokens: 16384` are declared explicitly for kimi (matches the catalog spec today, but immune to catalog drift); undeclared zai boots stay byte-identical.
- Artifact names (`tb-runs-shard-N`) intentionally unchanged — the merge job downloads by that pattern; run identity rides `run-name`/job name/summary header.

## How to verify

```bash
python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench   # 328 tests, incl. new ProviderResolveStepTest + shape tests
dart test test/cli/env_provider_preconfig_test.dart test/model_roles/provider_catalog_test.dart
actionlint .github/workflows/bench.yml                  # clean
```

Owner setup (E2E blocker, not the code): add the repo secret `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY`, then smoke `tasks=hello-world, provider=kimi-for-coding, 1 shard`.

Note: `dart test test/cli/` (full dir) passes all 245 tests but the VM aborts in glibc at process shutdown on this runner — reproduced identically on clean `origin/main` (pre-existing environment issue, unrelated to this change).

flowchart TD

  SEC1[secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY] --> RES

  RES -->|unknown choice / missing secret: [REDACTED:Sensitive Value] fail, zero shard-hours| X1((fail))
  RES -->|outputs: type, config JSON, key env, run_label| SHARD[bench shard jobs]
  SHARD -->|FA_PROVIDER_TYPE / FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG / key by name| AG[fa_agent.py → container env preconfig]
  AG --> MODEL[buildCliDefaultModel: declared contextWindow/maxTokens win]
  SHARD --> SUM[summary.py: Provider: run_label + pinned MODEL]

# pr-1475: gh-1471 [GOAL] bench.yml: provider selection for tbench runs (zai-glm default, kimi-for-coding) with a dedicated bench key

## Description

Closes #1471
## What changed

The terminal-bench workflow stops hardcoding the z.ai GLM provider: a new `provider` dispatch choice (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding`) is resolved in the setup job to the full provider triple and preflighted against the selected bench secret before any shard starts; kimi runs on a dedicated `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` (never `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY`) as `kimi` / `api.kimi.com/coding/v1` / `k3-256k`. The `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` env contract now accepts optional `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` (rides the resolver's override layer into the booted model), and the run identity (workflow `run-name`, shard job names via `needs` outputs, summary `Provider:` header via `BENCH_RUN_LABEL`) names provider+model. `bench/pricing.json` gains an explicit zero entry for `k3-256k` with a comment (subscription plan, no published per-token price — never an invented number).

## Key decisions

- Resolve + secret preflight live in the **setup job** (presence check only, key value never echoed; base64 form masked like the shard step's standing contract) — a bad dispatch fails in minute one, burning zero shard-hours; shard jobs consume the resolved outputs via `needs`.
- REG-1: the default choice resolves the exact legacy 3-field zai JSON (`model` still sourced from the `BENCH_MODEL` pin) — pinned byte-for-byte by a UT.
- Shard step maps **both** bench secrets and the run block picks the resolved key by name (`${!FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV}`) — no dynamic `secrets[...]` indexing, block stays env-driven and testable by the existing shell-harness family.
- `contextWindow: 200000` / `maxTokens: 16384` are declared explicitly for kimi (matches the catalog spec today, but immune to catalog drift); undeclared zai boots stay byte-identical.
- Artifact names (`tb-runs-shard-N`) intentionally unchanged — the merge job downloads by that pattern; run identity rides `run-name`/job name/summary header.

        description: 'gh-1471 D1/AC 2a: ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'

        description: 'Dataset spec passed to tb -d (name==version)'
        required: false

        description: 'Matrix shard count (10 tasks/shard on the 80-task core dataset)'
        required: false

        required: false

        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false

        description: 'Floor for declared task test timeouts, seconds (gh-1206; 0 = declared budgets)'
        required: false

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds up to 5 runners for hours; queue a second
# dispatch instead of stacking them.
concurrency:
  group: bench
  cancel-in-progress: false

# One source of truth for the bench model id (PR #1351 review): the run
# config and both summary steps must never drift apart — a stale copy is
# exactly the silent mispricing AC3 of issue #1339 fixes. (The job name
# cannot read this context — see the note on `name:` below.)
env:
  BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & resolve shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30

      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Round-3 review: validate max-concurrent like its siblings — 0 or
      # negative would spin the whole matrix as effectively unbounded
      # (and poison FA_BENCH_CONCURRENCY / the packing budget); fail the
      # dispatch BEFORE any bundle is built. (A non-integer value still
      # dies at workflow-graph parse — strategy.max-parallel fromJSON —
      # before any job starts; this guard catches everything numeric.)
      - name: Validate max-concurrent
        run: |
          case "${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}" in
            ''|*[!0-9]*)
              echo "::error::max-concurrent must be a positive integer, got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -lt 1 ] || [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -gt 8 ]; then
            echo "::error::max-concurrent must be between 1 and 8 (the split count), got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1
          fi

      # gh-1471: map the provider choice to the full provider triple
      # (type/baseUrl/model/key env) and preflight the selected secret
      # BEFORE the bundle builds or any shard starts — a missing
      # FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY must cost one setup minute, not 8 shards × hours
      # of 429s. Presence only: the value is never echoed (the ::add-mask
      # line masks its base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into
      # the container). An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a
      # silent fallthrough to the zai default.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY

              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;

              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Pins the knob/timeout shell logic of the bench.yml shard step (gh-1209).

The `run:` block decides, from two workflow_dispatch inputs, whether the
outer tb harness cap must sit above the progress ladder's ceiling and which
env vars reach fa_agent.py. This suite executes that exact block against a
`tb` stub and pins one behavior per input combination:

- REG-1 (issue #1122): both inputs absent → byte-for-byte stock delegation —
  no FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC, no FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION, no --global-agent-
  timeout-sec.
- gh-1209: any active ladder (explicit agent-timeout, or progress-extension
  on with its 360s default base) pins the harness cap at 4x base + 180s so
  the ladder decides, never the flat harness wait_for.
- gh-1209 review: `agent-timeout=0` is rejected at step start — it used to
  pass validation, export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC=0, and raise ValueError
  inside EVERY trial's perform_task hours into the shard.
- Invalid inputs (non-digit timeout, non-boolean extension) fail fast.

Issue #1406: the fa launch path must carry the ConnTrace env into the
tmux pane itself (string-level asserts on the generated TerminalCommand
— the exact bytes tb types into the pane), and a trial whose
bench_metrics.json folded zero requests despite real model usage must
fire a LOUD workflow warning, never ship an empty shell silently.

gh-1471: the setup-job provider resolve step maps the dispatch choice
(zai-glm-5.3-flash default / kimi-for-coding / custom) to the full
provider triple and preflights the selected secret BEFORE any shard
starts — each choice pins (type, baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar), an
unmapped value fails hard, a missing secret fails fast naming the
secret, and a key value never reaches the log. The custom path (D1 /
AC 2a) validates the provider-config JSON (parseable object, non-empty
https:// baseUrl + model, no key-like fields case-insensitively) and
injects the fixed apiKeyEnvVar FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM — the key comes only
from FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY. REG-1: the default's provider_config is
byte-identical to the pre-gh-1471 3-field zai JSON.

Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench
"""
import importlib.util
import collections
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import types
import unittest
from contextlib import redirect_stderr
from io import StringIO
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent
_BENCH_YML = _REPO_ROOT / ".github" / "workflows" / "bench.yml"
sys.path.insert(0, str(_REPO_ROOT / "bench"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

import bench_metrics  # noqa: E402


def _shard_run_block() -> str:
    """Extracts the `run: |` block of the tb shard step from bench.yml.

    Text-slicing, not PyYAML: the block is a literal scalar and the suite
    must run anywhere python3 runs (the bench shards have no PyYAML). The
    block is identified by its `tb run -d` body, so unrelated `run:` blocks
    never match.
    """
    lines = _BENCH_YML.read_text().splitlines()
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if line.strip() != "run: |":
            continue
        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
        body = []
        for candidate in lines[i + 1 :]:
            if candidate.strip() and (len(candidate) - len(candidate.lstrip())) <= indent:
                break
            body.append(candidate)
        while body and not body[-1].strip():
            body.pop()
        block = "\n".join(body)
        if "tb run -d" in block:
            start = True
            break
    else:
        raise AssertionError("tb shard step's run: | block not found in bench.yml")
    # Only expression the block may interpolate; anything else means the
    # workflow grew a new one and this harness needs the mapping extended.
    block = re.sub(r"\$\{\{\s*matrix\.i\s*\}\}", "0", block)
    leftover = re.findall(r"\$\{\{[^}]*\}\}", block)
    assert not leftover, f"unmapped GitHub expression(s) in run block: {leftover}"
    return block


def _resolve_run_block() -> str:
    """Extracts the `run: |` block of the gh-1471 provider resolve step.

    Same text-slicing contract as [_shard_run_block]: the block is
    identified by its body (the provider_config printf), so unrelated
    `run:` blocks never match. The block is env-driven (inputs/secrets
    arrive via the step env), so no GitHub expression may appear inside.
    """
    lines = _BENCH_YML.read_text().splitlines()
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if line.strip() != "run: |":
            continue
        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
        body = []
        for candidate in lines[i + 1 :]:
            if candidate.strip() and (len(candidate) - len(candidate.lstrip())) <= indent:
                break
            body.append(candidate)
        while body and not body[-1].strip():
            body.pop()
        block = "\n".join(body)
        if "provider_config=$(printf" in block:
            break
    else:
        raise AssertionError("provider resolve step's run: | block not found in bench.yml")
    leftover = re.findall(r"\$\{\{[^}]*\}\}", block)
    assert not leftover, f"unmapped GitHub expression(s) in resolve block: {leftover}"
    return block

# test reads the step outputs from it) and all three bench secrets in env
# (gh-1471 D1/AC 2a: the custom path preflights FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY).

The terminal-bench workflow stops hardcoding the z.ai GLM provider: a new `provider` dispatch choice (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding`) is resolved in the setup job to the full provider triple and preflighted against the selected bench secret before any shard starts; kimi runs on a dedicated `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` (never `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY`) as `kimi` / `api.kimi.com/coding/v1` / `k3-256k`. The terminal-bench workflow stops hardcoding the z.ai GLM provider: a new `provider` dispatch choice (`zai-glm-5.3-flash` default / `kimi-for-coding`) is resolved in the setup job to the full provider triple and preflighted against the selected bench secret before any shard starts; kimi runs on a dedicated `FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY` (never `KIMI_REVIEW_KEY`) as `kimi` / `api.kimi.com/coding/v1` / `k3-256k`. workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Task id or glob passed to tb -t (e.g. hello-world, crack-7z-hash*, * for the full dataset)'
        required: false
        default: 'hello-world'
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1471: default = todays behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'gh-1471 D1/AC 2a: ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Dataset spec passed to tb -d (name==version)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench-core==0.1.1'
      shards:
        description: 'Matrix shard count (10 tasks/shard on the 80-task core dataset)'
        required: false
        default: '8'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared caps, median 360s)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      test-timeout-floor:
        description: 'Floor for declared task test timeouts, seconds (gh-1206; 0 = declared budgets)'
        required: false
        default: '120'
      max-concurrent:
        description: 'Shard jobs running at once (issue #1392: split 8, run 2 — the ours-vs-endpoint experiment; GHA queues the rest)'
        required: false
        default: '2'

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds up to 5 runners for hours; queue a second
# dispatch instead of stacking them.
concurrency:
  group: bench
  cancel-in-progress: false

# One source of truth for the bench model id (PR #1351 review): the run
# config and both summary steps must never drift apart — a stale copy is
# exactly the silent mispricing AC3 of issue #1339 fixes. (The job name
# cannot read this context — see the note on `name:` below.)
env:
  BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & resolve shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Round-3 review: validate max-concurrent like its siblings — 0 or
      # negative would spin the whole matrix as effectively unbounded
      # (and poison FA_BENCH_CONCURRENCY / the packing budget); fail the
      # dispatch BEFORE any bundle is built. (A non-integer value still
      # dies at workflow-graph parse — strategy.max-parallel fromJSON —
      # before any job starts; this guard catches everything numeric.)
      - name: Validate max-concurrent
        run: |
          case "${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}" in
            ''|*[!0-9]*)
              echo "::error::max-concurrent must be a positive integer, got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -lt 1 ] || [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -gt 8 ]; then
            echo "::error::max-concurrent must be between 1 and 8 (the split count), got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1
          fi

      # gh-1471: map the provider choice to the full provider triple
      # (type/baseUrl/model/key env) and preflight the selected secret
      # BEFORE the bundle builds or any shard starts — a missing
      # FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY must cost one setup minute, not 8 shards × hours
      # of 429s. Presence only: the value is never echoed (the ::add-mask
      # line masks its base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into
      # the container). An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a
      # silent fallthrough to the zai default.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts.
              if ! printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -e 'type == "object"' >/dev/null 2>&1; then

# PR Discussion History

_Previous review discussions for PR #1475._

> ℹ️ **3 resolved thread(s) excluded; 7 machine notice(s) excluded (arming/status boilerplate — never reply targets).**

## Review Threads (Inline Comments)

### Thread 4 — `.github/workflows/bench.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
🚨 **BLOCKING: the custom path's `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` is rejected by the Dart env preconfig — every custom trial dies at container boot**

The custom arm builds the shard config with a verbatim passthrough plus the fixed key-env injection (line 280):

```bash
provider_config=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -c --arg k "$key_env" '. + {apiKeyEnvVar: $k}')
```

For the **documented** input shape (`provider-config: {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}`, per the input description and pinned by `test_custom_provider_config_flows_verbatim_with_fixed_key_env`), this produces:

```json
{"type":"openai","baseUrl":"https://api.example.com/v1","model":"m-1","contextWindow":128000,"maxTokens":8192,"apiKeyEnvVar":"FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM"}
```

The Dart consumer does not accept a `type` key inside `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG` — `_supportedConfigKeys` is `baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar, contextWindow, maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel` only. Verified against this branch:

```
ConfigException: unknown FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG key: "type" — supported keys: baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar, contextWindow, maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel
  package:flutter_agent_harness/src/cli/env_provider_preconfig.dart  _takeConfigEntry
```

And `faProviderPreconfig`'s contract is deliberate: *"a container that names its provider wrong must fail loud at boot"* — so a custom dispatch burns a whole shard of trials that all fail at fa boot. The run only works if the user **omits** `type` (then `.type // "openai"` sets `provider_type` with no `type` key in the JSON) — i.e. the opposite of the documented example.

Two sound fixes (pick one):

1. **Strip `type` in the passthrough** — it already rides the dedicated `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE` output/env:
   ```bash
   provider_config=$(printf '%s' "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" | jq -c --arg k "$key_env" 'del(.type) + {apiKeyEnvVar: $k}')
   ```
2. **Accept `type` Dart-side** — add it to `_supportedConfigKeys` and cross-check it equals the resolved `FA_PROVIDER_TYPE` (a mismatch would be a loud misconfiguration).

Either way, add one cross-layer test: feed the workflow resolve step's actual `provider_config` output into `parseEnvProviderPreconfig` (the two sides are currently pinned by separate tests with opposite expectations — which is exactly how this slipped through).

---

### Thread 5 — `.github/workflows/bench.yml`

**ai-teammate** (2026-10-10):
⚠️ **IMPORTANT: the custom preflight doesn't cover the config keys the Dart consumer will enforce — a bad dispatch burns shard-hours, not one setup minute**

The resolve step validates parseability, `baseUrl`/`model`, https-only, and key-like field names (all good), but the config then flows **verbatim** into `FA_PROVIDER_CONFIG`, where the Dart `_parseConfig` enforces a closed whitelist with typed validators:

- any key outside `baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar, contextWindow, maxTokens, input, thinkingLevel` (e.g. a typo'd `"baseurl"`, or an `"organization"` a provider doc suggested) passes this preflight and fails **loud inside every trial** after shards start;
- `contextWindow`/`maxTokens` below the resolver floors (`minOverrideContextWindow` 16384 / `minOverrideMaxTokens`) likewise pass preflight and throw at container boot;
- `.type` is used unchecked: `{"type": 123}` or `{"type": ""}` yields `provider_type` garbage/empty (jq `//` treats `""` as present) → the catalog lookup fails in the container instead of minute one.

The PR's own design goal is "a bad dispatch fails in minute one, burning zero shard-hours" — a one-block jq check at resolve time closes the gap (whitelist the keys, integer+floor the capability pair, string-check `type` when present), and would have made the `type`-key clash in the sibling finding impossible to miss. While there: the key-like scan only inspects top-level `keys[]` — a key nested inside an object value (e.g. `"headers": {"apiKey": [REDACTED:Sensitive Value]}`) rides through; scanning `.. | objects | keys[]` is a cheap widening (values can smuggle data regardless, but field-name paste accidents are what D1 targets).

#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Pins the knob/timeout shell logic of the bench.yml shard step (gh-1209).

The `run:` block decides, from two workflow_dispatch inputs, whether the
outer tb harness cap must sit above the progress ladder's ceiling and which
env vars reach fa_agent.py. This suite executes that exact block against a
`tb` stub and pins one behavior per input combination:

- REG-1 (issue #1122): both inputs absent → byte-for-byte stock delegation —
  no FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC, no FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION, no --global-agent-
  timeout-sec.
- gh-1209: any active ladder (explicit agent-timeout, or progress-extension
  on with its 360s default base) pins the harness cap at 4x base + 180s so
  the ladder decides, never the flat harness wait_for.
- gh-1209 review: `agent-timeout=0` is rejected at step start — it used to
  pass validation, export FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC=0, and raise ValueError
  inside EVERY trial's perform_task hours into the shard.
- Invalid inputs (non-digit timeout, non-boolean extension) fail fast.

Issue #1406: the fa launch path must carry the ConnTrace env into the
tmux pane itself (string-level asserts on the generated TerminalCommand
— the exact bytes tb types into the pane), and a trial whose
bench_metrics.json folded zero requests despite real model usage must
fire a LOUD workflow warning, never ship an empty shell silently.

gh-1471: the setup-job provider resolve step maps the dispatch choice
(zai-glm-5.3-flash default / kimi-for-coding / custom) to the full
provider triple and preflights the selected secret BEFORE any shard
starts — each choice pins (type, baseUrl, model, apiKeyEnvVar), an
unmapped value fails hard, a missing secret fails fast naming the
secret, and a key value never reaches the log. The custom path (D1 /
AC 2a) validates the provider-config JSON (parseable object, non-empty
https:// baseUrl + model, no key-like fields case-insensitively) and
injects the fixed apiKeyEnvVar FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM — the key comes only
from FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY. REG-1: the default's provider_config is
byte-identical to the pre-gh-1471 3-field zai JSON.

Run: python3 -m unittest discover -s bench/terminal_bench
"""
import importlib.util
import collections
import json
import os
import re
import shutil
import subprocess
import sys
import tempfile
import types
import unittest
from contextlib import redirect_stderr
from io import StringIO
from pathlib import Path
from unittest import mock

_REPO_ROOT = Path(__file__).resolve().parent.parent.parent
_BENCH_YML = _REPO_ROOT / ".github" / "workflows" / "bench.yml"
sys.path.insert(0, str(_REPO_ROOT / "bench"))
sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))

import bench_metrics  # noqa: E402


def _shard_run_block() -> str:
    """Extracts the `run: |` block of the tb shard step from bench.yml.

    Text-slicing, not PyYAML: the block is a literal scalar and the suite
    must run anywhere python3 runs (the bench shards have no PyYAML). The
    block is identified by its `tb run -d` body, so unrelated `run:` blocks
    never match.
    """
    lines = _BENCH_YML.read_text().splitlines()
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if line.strip() != "run: |":
            continue
        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
        body = []
        for candidate in lines[i + 1 :]:
            if candidate.strip() and (len(candidate) - len(candidate.lstrip())) <= indent:
                break
            body.append(candidate)
        while body and not body[-1].strip():
            body.pop()
        block = "\n".join(body)
        if "tb run -d" in block:
            start = True
            break
    else:
        raise AssertionError("tb shard step's run: | block not found in bench.yml")
    # Only expression the block may interpolate; anything else means the
    # workflow grew a new one and this harness needs the mapping extended.
    block = re.sub(r"\$\{\{\s*matrix\.i\s*\}\}", "0", block)
    leftover = re.findall(r"\$\{\{[^}]*\}\}", block)
    assert not leftover, f"unmapped GitHub expression(s) in run block: {leftover}"
    return block


def _resolve_run_block() -> str:
    """Extracts the `run: |` block of the gh-1471 provider resolve step.

    Same text-slicing contract as [_shard_run_block]: the block is
    identified by its body (the provider_config printf), so unrelated
    `run:` blocks never match. The block is env-driven (inputs/secrets
    arrive via the step env), so no GitHub expression may appear inside.
    """
    lines = _BENCH_YML.read_text().splitlines()
    for i, line in enumerate(lines):
        if line.strip() != "run: |":
            continue
        indent = len(line) - len(line.lstrip())
        body = []
        for candidate in lines[i + 1 :]:
            if candidate.strip() and (len(candidate) - len(candidate.lstrip())) <= indent:
                break
            body.append(candidate)
        while body and not body[-1].strip():
            body.pop()
        block = "\n".join(body)
        if "provider_config=$(printf" in block:
            break
    else:
        raise AssertionError("provider resolve step's run: | block not found in bench.yml")
    leftover = re.findall(r"\$\{\{[^}]*\}\}", block)
    assert not leftover, f"unmapped GitHub expression(s) in resolve block: {leftover}"
    return block

# test reads the step outputs from it) and all three bench secrets in env
# (gh-1471 D1/AC 2a: the custom path preflights FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY).

def _run_resolve(
    provider="",
    zai_key="zai-test-key",
    kimi_key="kimi-test-key",
    custom_key="custom-test-key",
    provider_config="",
):
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env.update(
        {
            "PROVIDER": provider,
            "BENCH_MODEL": "glm-5.3-flash",
            "PROVIDER_CONFIG": provider_config,
            "FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY": zai_key,
            "FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY": kimi_key,
            "FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY": custom_key,
        }
    )
    tmp = tempfile.TemporaryDirectory()
    output = Path(tmp.name) / "github_output"
    env["GITHUB_OUTPUT"] = str(output)
    driver = Path(tmp.name) / "resolve_step.sh"
    driver.write_text("#!/usr/bin/env bash\n" + _resolve_run_block() + "\n")
    proc = subprocess.run(
        ["bash", str(driver)],
        env=env,
        capture_output=True,
        text=True,
        timeout=30,
    )
    proc._tmp = tmp  # caller cleans up after reading the outputs
    proc.github_output = output
    return proc


def _resolve_outputs(proc) -> dict:
    if not proc.github_output.exists():
        return {}
    result = {}
    for line in proc.github_output.read_text().splitlines():
        if "=" in line:
            key, _, value = line.partition("=")
            result[key] = value
    proc._tmp.cleanup()
    return result


# The tb stub records the exact argv the block computed plus the two env
# vars fa_agent.py's TimeoutKnobs reads, then exits 0 — the real tb never
# runs in tests.
_TB_STUB = r"""
tb() {
  echo "TB_BEGIN"
  local a
  for a in "$@"; do echo "arg:$a"; done
  echo "TB_END"
  echo "FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC=${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_SEC-__unset__}"
  echo "FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION=${FA_PROGRESS_EXTENSION-__unset__}"
  echo "FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC=${FA_AGENT_TIMEOUT_ABS_CEILING_SEC-__unset__}"
}
"""

_DRIVER = "#!/usr/bin/env bash\n" + _TB_STUB + "\n" + _shard_run_block() + "\n"


def _run_shard(agent_timeout="", progress_extension=""):
    env = dict(os.environ)
    env.update(
        {
            "DATASET": "/tmp/fa-bench-workflow-test-dataset",
            "SHARD_TASKS": "task-0 task-1",
            "FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI": "test-key",
            # gh-1471: the resolve step (setup job) names the key env var
            # for the run block's indirection; the zai default names the
            # zai var.
            "FA_PROVIDER_KEY_ENV": "FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI",
            "AGENT_TIMEOUT": agent_timeout,
            "PROGRESS_EXTENSION": progress_extension,
        }
    )
    with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as tmp:
        driver = Path(tmp) / "shard_step.sh"
        driver.write_text(_DRIVER)
        proc = subprocess.run(
            ["bash", str(driver)],
            env=env,
            capture_output=True,
            text=True,
            timeout=30,
        )
    return proc


def _tb_args(stdout):
    args = []
    inside = False
    for line in stdout.splitlines():
        if line == "TB_BEGIN":
            inside = True
        elif line == "TB_END":
            inside = False
        elif inside and line.startswith("arg:"):
            args.append(line[len("arg:") :])
    return args


def _env_value(stdout, name):
    for line in stdout.splitlines():
        if line.startswith(name + "="):
            return line[len(name) + 1 :]
    return None


def _flag_value(args, flag):
    return args[args.index(flag) + 1] if flag in args else None


@unittest.skipUnless(
    _BENCH_YML.exists(), "bench.yml not found (standalone bench checkout)"
)

workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      tasks:
        description: 'Task id or glob passed to tb -t (e.g. hello-world, crack-7z-hash*, * for the full dataset)'
        required: false
        default: 'hello-world'
      provider:
        description: 'LLM provider for this run (gh-1471: default = todays behavior bit-for-bit; kimi needs the FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY secret; custom needs FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY + provider-config)'
        required: false
        default: 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
        type: choice
        options:
          - 'zai-glm-5.3-flash'
          - 'kimi-for-coding'
          - 'custom'
      provider-config:
        description: 'gh-1471 D1/AC 2a: ONLY when provider=custom — the provider config JSON {"type","baseUrl","model","contextWindow","maxTokens"}. The API key NEVER rides this input (run metadata is visible) — it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY secret'
        required: false
        default: ''
      dataset:
        description: 'Dataset spec passed to tb -d (name==version)'
        required: false
        default: 'terminal-bench-core==0.1.1'
      shards:
        description: 'Matrix shard count (10 tasks/shard on the 80-task core dataset)'
        required: false
        default: '8'
      agent-timeout:
        description: 'Base agent cap seconds (issue #1122; absent = dataset-declared caps, median 360s)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      progress-extension:
        description: 'Extend the agent cap while the agent output grows (idle window 120s, hard ceiling 4x base)'
        required: false
        default: ''
      test-timeout-floor:
        description: 'Floor for declared task test timeouts, seconds (gh-1206; 0 = declared budgets)'
        required: false
        default: '120'
      max-concurrent:
        description: 'Shard jobs running at once (issue #1392: split 8, run 2 — the ours-vs-endpoint experiment; GHA queues the rest)'
        required: false
        default: '2'

permissions:
  contents: read

# A full-dataset run holds up to 5 runners for hours; queue a second
# dispatch instead of stacking them.
concurrency:
  group: bench
  cancel-in-progress: false

# One source of truth for the bench model id (PR #1351 review): the run
# config and both summary steps must never drift apart — a stale copy is
# exactly the silent mispricing AC3 of issue #1339 fixes. (The job name
# cannot read this context — see the note on `name:` below.)
env:
  BENCH_MODEL: glm-5.3-flash

jobs:
  setup:
    name: Build bundle & resolve shards
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    timeout-minutes: 30
    outputs:
      matrix: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.matrix }}
      count: ${{ steps.shards.outputs.count }}
      provider_type: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_type }}
      provider_config: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_config }}
      provider_key_env: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.provider_key_env }}
      bench_model: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.bench_model }}
      run_label: ${{ steps.provider.outputs.run_label }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1

      # Round-3 review: validate max-concurrent like its siblings — 0 or
      # negative would spin the whole matrix as effectively unbounded
      # (and poison FA_BENCH_CONCURRENCY / the packing budget); fail the
      # dispatch BEFORE any bundle is built. (A non-integer value still
      # dies at workflow-graph parse — strategy.max-parallel fromJSON —
      # before any job starts; this guard catches everything numeric.)
      - name: Validate max-concurrent
        run: |
          case "${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}" in
            ''|*[!0-9]*)
              echo "::error::max-concurrent must be a positive integer, got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1 ;;
          esac
          if [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -lt 1 ] || [ "$((10#${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}))" -gt 8 ]; then
            echo "::error::max-concurrent must be between 1 and 8 (the split count), got '${{ inputs.max-concurrent }}'"; exit 1
          fi

      # gh-1471: map the provider choice to the full provider triple
      # (type/baseUrl/model/key env) and preflight the selected secret
      # BEFORE the bundle builds or any shard starts — a missing
      # FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY must cost one setup minute, not 8 shards × hours
      # of 429s. Presence only: the value is never echoed (the ::add-mask
      # line masks its base64 form, the transport fa_agent.py uses into
      # the container). An unmapped provider value fails hard — never a
      # silent fallthrough to the zai default.
      - name: Resolve provider
        id: provider
        env:
          PROVIDER: ${{ inputs.provider }}
          PROVIDER_CONFIG: ${{ inputs.provider-config }}
          BENCH_MODEL: ${{ env.BENCH_MODEL }}
          FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY }}
          FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY: ${{ secrets.FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          case "$PROVIDER" in
            ''|zai-glm-5.3-flash)
              provider_type=zai
              choice=zai-glm-5.3-flash
              base_url='https://api.z.ai/api/coding/paas/v4'
              model="$BENCH_MODEL"
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_Z_AI_Z_AI
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_ZAI_KEY
              # REG-1 (gh-1471): the default must resolve today's exact
              # 3-field config — a zai run stays byte-identical.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s"}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              # D5: one spelling everywhere — the label derives from the
              # dispatch choice id, matching run-name.
              run_label="$choice ($model)"
              ;;
            kimi-for-coding)
              provider_type=kimi
              base_url='https://api.kimi.com/coding/v1'
              model='k3-256k'
              key_env=FA_KEY_API_KIMI_COM_BENCH
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_KIMI_KEY
              # gh-1471 D4: kimi's capability fields ride the config
              # explicitly — the env preconfig applies them to the booted
              # model, so a catalog drift can never silently truncate.
              provider_config=$(printf '{"baseUrl":"%s","model":"%s","apiKeyEnvVar":"%s","contextWindow":200000,"maxTokens":16384}' \
                "$base_url" "$model" "$key_env")
              run_label="kimi-for-coding ($model)"
              ;;
            custom)
              # gh-1471 D1 / AC 2a: the custom escape hatch — a new
              # provider tomorrow needs zero workflow edits. The key
              # NEVER rides the dispatch input (inputs are visible in
              # run metadata): it comes only from the FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              # secret, injected as the fixed apiKeyEnvVar below.
              secret_name=FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              secret_value=$FA_BENCH_CUSTOM_KEY
              key_env=FA_KEY_BENCH_CUSTOM
              if [ -z "$PROVIDER_CONFIG" ]; then
                echo "::error::provider custom selected but the provider-config input is empty — pass the provider JSON (at least baseUrl and model)"; exit 1
              fi
              # jq-level validation (AC 2a): every failure names the
              # offending input and dies BEFORE any shard starts.

# PR Discussion History
